newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police ban Megawati commemoration.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police ban Megawati commemoration.

text.p: Indonesian police have banned supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri from commemorating last year's raid on party offices which led to a major riot, the Jakarta Post reported on Friday.

Megawati loyalists were planning to offer prayers at her house on Saturday and lay wreaths on Sunday at the site of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) headquarters in Central Jakarta which was raided last July 27 by supporters of her government-backed party rival Surjadi as well as police and troops.

According to a report by the official National Commission of Human Rights, at least five people died, 23 went missing and 149 were injured in rioting sparked by the raid. It criticised the interference of security forces in political matters.
It was the worst rioting in the capital for more than two decades.
The Jakarta Post quoted national police spokesman Colonel Bambang Haryoko as saying the planned event was likely to pose security problems because a large number of people would be involved.
"The commemoration is likely to create a security problem. Experience shows that mass gatherings can easily turn violent and are difficult to handle," Haryoko was quoted as saying.
Last year's raid took place after Megawati supporters refused to leave PDI headquarters more than a month after she had been deposed as party chief by Surjadi at a government-funded congress.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, still regards herself as the PDI leader.
The Merdeka daily on Friday quoted Megawati supporter Haryanto Taslam as saying Megawati's excessive board had sent a letter to police notifying them of the planned activities.
"The executive board did not ask for permission, but we did inform the police that the people of Jakarta, especially PDI members and sympathisers, will commemorate the July 27 event," Taslam said.
Despite her ousting, Megawati still has considerable influence over PDI supporters as demonstrated during the May general elections, from which she was barred from participating.
Analysts say her public pronouncement that she would not vote led to a collapse of the PDI vote from about 15 percent to around three percent nationally.

The ruling Golkar party won the poll with a record majority in excess of 74 percent, while the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) picked up the balance. Only the three parties were permitted to contest the poll.
